findings.claim: Chest pain is a listed sign of cardiac distress presuming contraindication of other transport.
findings.quote: Exhibits signs and symptoms of acute respiratory distress or cardiac distress such as shortness of breath or chest pain
findings.case_fact: The ambulance report states that the beneficiary was being transported due to chest pain.

findings.claim: Multiple therapy disciplines required; PT and OT both provided.
findings.quote: the patient required the active and ongoing therapeutic intervention of multiple therapy disciplines
findings.case_fact: Physical therapy totaling 60-90 minutes per day was provided every weekday.

findings.claim: Intensity standard of 3 hours/day 5 days/week asserted as met.
findings.quote: intensive therapies at least 3 hours per day at least 5 days per week
findings.case_fact: the patient received three hours daily of therapy services

findings.claim: Measurable improvement shown.
findings.quote: the patient can reasonably be expected to make measurable improvement
findings.case_fact: I.W. had succeeded in raising all her ADL levels, most of them to her goal level

findings.claim: Physician contact asserted daily, exceeding 3 days/week.
findings.quote: the rehabilitation physician must conduct face-to-face visits with the patient at least 3 days per week
findings.case_fact: daily direct contact by a physiatrist throughout the patient’s stay

findings.claim: Caregiver already gives oral meds and insulin; nurse administration of oral meds is not skilled absent complexity, none shown.
findings.quote: The administration of oral medications by a nurse is not reasonable and necessary skilled nursing care except in the specific situation
findings.case_fact: the beneficiary had a caregiver who provided assistance with activities of daily living as well as the administration of oral medications and injections of insulin

findings.claim: Beneficiaries were stable at discharge; no ongoing instability shown to justify skilled observation.
findings.quote: Skilled observation and monitoring of the patient's blood pressure and medication regimen is required until the blood pressure remains stable and in a safe range
findings.case_fact: based on the general stability of his blood sugar, blood pressure and overall control of his conditions

findings.claim: Coumadin dosage was being adjusted, so prothrombin monitoring is reasonable and necessary.
findings.quote: Where the documentation shows that the dosage is being adjusted, monitoring would be reasonable and necessary
findings.case_fact: based on this data, his physician modified the Coumadin dosages twice

findings.claim: Skilled observation justified while regimen unstable (INR above safe range).
findings.quote: Skilled observation and monitoring of the patient's blood pressure and medication regimen is required until the blood pressure remains stable and in a safe range
findings.case_fact: well above the safe range on December 11, 2008

findings.claim: Plan of care specified services and frequency.
findings.quote: The orders on the plan of care must indicate the type of services to be provided to the patient
findings.case_fact: ordered skilled nursing care once in the initial week and then twice a week for four weeks

findings.claim: Passage only defines BLS as medically necessary services; no passage supplies the test that other transport was contraindicated, so the nausea/caregiver facts cannot be resolved.
findings.quote: When medically necessary, the provision of BLS services
findings.case_fact: Testimony presented during the hearing indicated that transport was in fact due to nausea

findings.claim: Patient was treated and released; no emergency criteria in the passages to apply.
findings.quote: the provision of medically necessary supplies and services
findings.case_fact: the beneficiary was treated and released

findings.claim: Air ambulance requires condition needing rapid transport that ground could not provide; appellant concedes ground was reasonable.
findings.quote: The beneficiary’s medical condition required immediate and rapid ambulance transportation that could not have been provided by ground ambulance
findings.case_fact: the appellant concedes that “ground transportation to a closer hospital was reasonable” in this case

findings.claim: Patient was stable at transfer, not showing need for air transport.
findings.quote: approve claims only if the beneficiary’s medical condition is such that transportation by either basic or advanced life support ground ambulance is not appropriate
findings.case_fact: The beneficiary’s vital signs were stable at the time of transfer

findings.claim: A closer equipped facility existed.
findings.quote: Great distances or other obstacles are involved in getting the patient to the nearest hospital with appropriate facilities
findings.case_fact: there was a closer facility equipped to treat the beneficiary’s medical needs

findings.claim: Coverage only to nearest hospital capable of required care; neurosurgeon recommended Neuro ICU, but whether a nearer capable facility existed is not stated.
findings.quote: covered under Part B as an ambulance service only to the nearest hospital, critical access hospital (CAH)
findings.case_fact: who recommended that the beneficiary be transferred to the “St. Francis Neuro ICU.”

findings.claim: Family preference alone would not suffice; record shows physician-recommended transfer for neurosurgical evaluation.
findings.quote: Coverage is not available for transport from a hospital capable of treating the patient
findings.case_fact: The ER physician documented that he consulted with the neurosurgeon on call

findings.claim: Necessity requires that other transport be contraindicated; cardiologist says monitored ambulance was absolutely necessary.
findings.quote: Medical necessity is established when the patient's condition is such that use of any other method of transportation is contraindicated.
findings.case_fact: it was “absolutely necessary” to take him from the hospital to the rehabilitation center by ambulance with a cardiac monitor

findings.claim: Run sheet notes he could stand and walk, conflicting with need; passage says no payment if other transport could be used without endangering health.
findings.quote: In any case in which some means of transportation other than an ambulance could be used without endangering the individual's health
findings.case_fact: Pt. was weak but could stand and walk on his own strength.

findings.claim: Multiple therapy disciplines (PT and OT) planned daily.
findings.quote: the patient required the active and ongoing therapeutic intervention of multiple therapy disciplines
findings.case_fact: providing daily occupational and physical therapy

findings.claim: Measurable improvement expected and achieved.
findings.quote: the patient can reasonably be expected to make measurable improvement
findings.case_fact: had moved from total assist for walking to modified independence in walking

findings.claim: Intensity (3 hours/day or 15 hours/week) is not stated in the case facts.
findings.quote: at least 3 hours of therapy per day at least 5 days per week
findings.case_fact: providing daily occupational and physical therapy

findings.claim: Physician face-to-face supervision at least 3 days/week is not stated in the case facts.
findings.quote: the rehabilitation physician must conduct face-to-face visits with the patient at least 3 days per week
findings.case_fact: By the end of her two-week stay in the IRF

findings.claim: Passages address inpatient admission orders; record shows status changed back to observation, but no passage covers the SNF coverage criteria.
findings.quote: may act as a proxy for the ordering practitioner provided they are authorized under state law to admit patients
findings.case_fact: Decision to change from observation to inpt status was made in ERROR.

findings.claim: Discharge summary says overnight observation only.
findings.quote: approves and accepts responsibility for the admission decision
findings.case_fact: was admitted for overnight observation

findings.claim: Part B covers transport only to nearest hospital, CAH or SNF; destination was recorded as a clinic.
findings.quote: only to the nearest hospital, critical access hospital (CAH), or skilled nursing facility (SNF)
findings.case_fact: On the ambulance run sheet, the destination to which the appellant was taken was described as a “clinic.”

findings.claim: Transport to a physician-directed clinic is not covered; appellant offers no support that it was a hospital or SNF.
findings.quote: Ambulance service to a physician’s office or a physician-directed clinic is not covered.
findings.case_fact: the clinic to which he was taken on the date of service was not a doctor’s office

findings.claim: Infrequent absences do not disqualify homebound status.
findings.quote: shall not so disqualify an individual if the absence is of an infrequent or of relatively short duration.
findings.case_fact: absences from the home, though infrequent, included adult day care and doctor visits

findings.claim: Recertification documents taxing effort and functional limitations.
findings.quote: longitudinal clinical information about the patient’s health status is typically needed
findings.case_fact: the beneficiary was unable to leave the home without taxing efforts

findings.claim: Passages cover admission orders and non-covered services, not clinical necessity of the inpatient stay; case shows observation then inpatient status.
findings.quote: The admission order is evidence of the decision by the ordering practitioner to admit the beneficiary to inpatient status.
findings.case_fact: He was initially placed in observation status but subsequently admitted to inpatient status.

findings.claim: Transferring hospital lacked cardiologists, meeting the inadequate facilities element.
findings.quote: the transferring hospital does not have adequate facilities to provide the medical services needed by the patient
findings.case_fact: The transfer occurred so that the beneficiary would be treated in a hospital where specialist cardiologist services were available.

findings.claim: Coverage requires the destination be the nearest appropriate hospital; appellant implies a Texas facility preferred by Medicare was not tried, and ground endangerment is not documented.
findings.quote: covered only if the hospital to which the patient is transferred is the nearest one with appropriate facilities.
findings.case_fact: before trying the facility in TX that Medicare preferred

findings.claim: SLP coverage turns on need for skilled care, not only improvement potential.
findings.quote: Coverage of speech-language pathology services is not determined solely on the presence or absence of a beneficiary’s potential for improvement
findings.case_fact: asserted that overall they did not expect his prognosis from the traumatic brain injury “overall” to improve significantly

findings.claim: Swallowing/feeding therapy expected to improve feeding ability and was shown to.
findings.quote: it is reasonably expected that the skilled service will improve, maintain, or prevent or slow further deterioration in the patient’s ability
findings.case_fact: The therapy notes of the second four week period record “steady improvements,”

findings.claim: Observation is covered only with reasonable potential for change/complication documented; facts show long-standing care for hypertension with no instability described.
findings.quote: Observation and assessment of the patient's condition by a nurse are reasonable and necessary skilled services where there is a reasonable potential for change
findings.case_fact: Her primary diagnosis was hypertension, and her other diagnoses were coronary atherosclerosis, cardiac dysrhythmia, polyarthritis, constipation, and urinary tract infection.

findings.claim: Skilled observation justified only until condition or regimen has stabilized; care ran about sixteen months.
findings.quote: until the patient's clinical condition and/or treatment regimen has stabilized
findings.case_fact: started care with the home health agency on June 15, 2003, approximately sixteen months before the dates of service at issue here

findings.claim: Day care absences are acceptable only if the center is licensed/certified; case does not say the county-sponsored center is.
findings.quote: an adult day care center must be either licensed or certified by the State or accredited by a private accrediting body
findings.case_fact: at an adult day care center, sponsored by a county mental health/mental retardation program

findings.claim: Aide personal care is covered when patient cannot do it, but nurse notes she moves independently.
findings.quote: Home health aide visits at an appropriate frequency would be reasonable and necessary to assist in these tasks.
findings.case_fact: moves in bed and in chair independently and has sufficient muscle strength to lift up completely during move

findings.claim: Nurse visits to fill a mediplanner and oversee aides are not skilled; nurse supervision unnecessary where aide tasks are unskilled.
findings.quote: Where visits by a licensed nurse are not needed to observe and assess the effects of the unskilled services being provided
findings.case_fact: a skilled nurse visited the beneficiary approximately once every two weeks to fill a mediplanner with pills and oversee home health aides

findings.claim: Aide hours exceed 28/week part-time limit.
findings.quote: 28 or fewer hours each week
findings.case_fact: averaging 30-35 hours a week, to assist with personal care, light housekeeping, and meal preparation

findings.claim: No skilled rehabilitation therapy; no change in condition showing potential for complication.
findings.quote: where there is a reasonable potential for change in a patient's condition
findings.case_fact: The beneficiary did not receive any skilled rehabilitation therapy during the period of service at issue.

findings.claim: Passages cover services related to non-covered services and private room isolation, not necessity of inpatient admission; the admission was for a covered hernia repair with pulmonary comorbidity.
findings.quote: Services "not related to" non-covered services are covered under Medicare.
findings.case_fact: her underlying pulmonary status

findings.claim: Pressure sore care is skilled when a nurse's skills are needed.
findings.quote: Care of wounds, (including, but not limited to, ulcers, burns, pressure sores, open surgical sites, fistulas, tube sites, and tumor erosion sites)
findings.case_fact: the provider’s nurses observed and assessed the pressure ulcer on the beneficiary’s sacrum; provided wound care

findings.claim: Diabetes can adversely affect healing, supporting skilled wound care.
findings.quote: has a reasonable potential to adversely affect healing (e.g., diabetes)
findings.case_fact: a principal diagnosis of type II diabetes, uncomplicated

findings.claim: Nurse taught caregiver and wounds healed, consistent with skilled teaching and monitoring.
findings.quote: the wound may still require skilled monitoring for signs and symptoms of infection or complication
findings.case_fact: PCA [personal care aide] was taught how to do the dressing change.

findings.quote: including when the services needed do not require skilled nursing care because they could safely and effectively be performed by the patient or unskilled caregivers
findings.case_fact: The Plan of Care indicates that the beneficiary's family administered her medications without problems

findings.claim: Clinical notes must clearly document the need for skilled care; case relies on assertions and two glucose readings.
findings.quote: Vague or subjective descriptions of the patient’s care should not be used.
findings.case_fact: The appellant references two blood glucose readings and edema of the beneficiary's lower extremities in support of its contentions.

findings.claim: Gait training is skilled and necessary if it can materially improve ability to walk.
findings.quote: are considered reasonable and necessary if they can be expected to materially improve or maintain the patient's ability to walk
findings.case_fact: to increase the beneficiary’s range of motion, manage pain, provide gait training

findings.claim: Objective measure improved, showing improvement.
findings.quote: The patient’s response to therapy must be documented.
findings.case_fact: Upon discharge, this score had improved to 18/28, signifying a moderate fall risk.
